correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 23–60: the hoppings converge to 1, giving a compact perturbation of the free half-line operator with essential spectrum [−2,2]. Outside that interval the recurrence starting at site zero gives simplicity, and alternating signs give exact reflection. Deleting interblock bonds costs at most two per cut for strict threshold counts. The exact constant-hopping cosine count with rounding error at most one and a 2Δ norm bound apply on each block. Below ε^(−1/3) a dimension bound suffices; the dyadic blocks up to η/ε have O_s(√m+1) counts apiece by comparison to the free block at threshold 2−C_s/m. The terminal tail beyond (s+η)/ε has norm below 2+ε. On the remaining scaled compact interval the uniform expansion 2a_n=2+sε/x+O_{s,η}(εδ+ε²) and the two shifted thresholds give upper and lower Riemann sums, with continuous positive-part square root even at the turning point. The omitted small-x integral is O_s(√η); substituting x=s sin²u gives the normalized integral s/2. Strict monotone count inversion gives the coefficient s²/4 in the j-law; a jump at an equality threshold changes the count by only one because of simplicity. The frozen checker was read, not run; its finite truncations test consistency, not the limit. No claim about the top eigenvalue or parameter uniformity is proved or needed.

In the DLMF recurrence put (λ,a_P,b_P,c)=(1,0,−g/2,0) and double the Jacobi operator: this gives unit hoppings and diagonal g/(n+1). Equation 18.35.6_4 and reflection 18.35.2_5 give exterior levels E_j=√(4+g²/j²), j≥1. Independent check: for E>2 the generating function of the half-line recurrence solves (1−Ez+z²)f'=(E−g−2z)f; at the root r∈(0,1) its exponent is g/√(E²−4)−1, so exactly the stated nonnegative-integer exponents give ℓ² eigenvectors.

Scaling the diagonal comparator to kinetic κ gives normalized count g/(2√κ), which is stable under the required relative bounds. The strict threshold, inverse j-law, and negative side are equivalent consequences here.

value.rationale: The operator and edge invariant are natural, and the frozen proof is a usable elementary exposition. But as an asserted exact new result, the coefficient is a direct evaluation of an already available general Coulomb formula at κ=1,g=s. The inverse eigenvalue and symmetry statements are routine consequences, and neither the motivating top-eigenvalue problem nor a refined error or uniform law is addressed. The specialization alone supplies no independent mathematical gain warranting acceptance.
